body:
I don't know if I can be more specific:
- when I don't specify the default config name like this Email::__construct(), I can't use the send method, I got this error

```
Fatal Error
Error: Call to a member function send() on a non-object 
File /var/www/website/vendor/cakephp/cakephp/src/Network/Email/Email.php    
Line: 1227
Notice: If you want to customize this error message, create src/Template/Error/fatal_error.ctp
```
- when I do specify the default config name in the constructor like this Email::__construct('default), I got this:

```
Could not send email: unknown
Error: An Internal Error Has Occurred.
Stack Trace
CORE/src/Network/Email/MailTransport.php line 52 → Cake\Network\Email\MailTransport->_mail(string, string, string, string, null)
```

I use the simple mail as transport. Also tried the deliver static method it didn't work.

When the email instance is built transport() should be called with the transport name. This should set the `_transport` property up correctly. It would seem that is not happening though. I can look at this tonight when I get home.

Thx you all. @luke83 with this config, I still catch a socket expection from the MailTransport class (the unknown error as mentioned above). My variables seems  correct though: 
$to:

```
/src/Network/Email/MailTransport.php (line 69)
'noff@noff.net'
```

$subject: 

```
/src/Network/Email/MailTransport.php (line 70)
'Registration'
```

$message:

```
/src/Network/Email/MailTransport.php (line 71)
'
To finish the registration and activate your account click here
'
```

$headers

```
/src/Network/Email/MailTransport.php (line 72)
'From: Hello <noreply@mywebsite.net>
X-Mailer: CakePHP Email
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2014 21:15:13 +0000
Message-ID: <53c599e1b4484d879cae0879c0a83865@factory.dev>
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit'
```

$params:

```
/src/Network/Email/MailTransport.php (line 73)
null
```

I also noticed the fact that you have to specify the template to use with Email::template('default') to populate the $message variable is this the expected behavior?
@luke83 thx for your insights. You're right a got an issue on server side configuration, I'll try to fix it

I tried to reproduce this locally and was unsuccessful. I was able to send email fine using the SmtpTransport and the code @luke83 provided. As @luke83 noted using `new Email('default');` is required if you do not want to use the `profile()` method. I'm hesitant to change the default argument as we ran into issues doing that in 2.x.

I agree that the fatal error is a bit terrible, and will fix that sending without a transport provides a more helpful error message.
All right guys thx a bunch

issue.title: Add a more helpful error message when the transport is undefined.
